title: The ‘ebb-and-flow’ distance illusion
abstract: Two dots can appear to approach and recede from each other even when their physical separation is constant. In our stimulus, a central dot is surrounded by grey discs whose diameters expand and contract while the whole configuration translates back and forth, resembling the Dynamic Ebbinghaus display. During disc expansion (and one translation direction), the dots often look closer together, whereas during disc contraction (and the opposite translation direction), they look farther apart. A set of informal demonstrations suggests that translation of the entire configuration is necessary. The effect weakens when either disc-diameter change or dot–disc-centre spacing change is removed, and it largely disappears when translation and disc dynamics are shifted by half a cycle. With as few as two surrounding discs, the illusion remains robust.
